rationale: Evidence from iteration 10 (score 896.7, best so far): the oval (20/20, 1.89 s, max_error 0.006 m) and s-bend (20/20, steering_oscillation 0.22) both finish reliably. The slalom has improved to 15/20 finishes with mean progress 0.94 and 0.35 line-loss events per run. Across the derivative sweep on the slalom, mean progress went 0.23 (kd 0.8), 0.42 (kd 1.1), 0.47 (kd 1.5), 0.67 (kd 1.8, base_speed 0.95), 0.94 (kd 2.4). Steering_oscillation has stayed flat as kd rose (oval 0.25, s-bend 0.22), so there is no sign yet that the derivative term is amplifying sensor noise. Geometry is fixed because every geometry change in iterations 4 to 6 hurt the score. Change: kd 2.4 to 2.8, with everything else held (geometry, kp 2.2, ki 0.15, base_speed 0.95, last_direction line loss). This is a single-variable step along the trend, which is the lowest-risk change for the final unseen-track race. Hypothesis H1: slalom failures are still lag at sharp alternations, so more damping lifts slalom finish rate toward 0.9 and cuts off-track exits. H2: oval and s-bend stay stable, since their steering_oscillation has not risen with kd. H3 (risk): at kd 2.8 noise amplification pushes steering_oscillation above about 0.4 on the s-bend or drops oval completions. The final race is unseen and cannot be followed up, so if the iteration-10 design is at least as robust, the risk is worth little; the gain on the development slalom is the main reason for the step. Expected result: slalom finish rate 0.85 or more, oval and s-bend 20/20, score about 920 or more. Measurements wanted: completion and progress on the slalom, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and max_error on all tracks, and noise_robustness to check whether noise is becoming the limit.
